ordered_diagnoses: Tooth impaction due to odontogenic lesion

facts.raw_span: A 22-year-old woman presented for evaluation of malaligned teeth
all permanent teeth had erupted except the third molars in both arches and the lower left lateral incisor
mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region
no history of prior dental extractions
an unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, which appeared to obstruct the eruption path of the tooth
A 22-year-old woman presented for evaluation of malaligned teeth
all permanent teeth had erupted except the third molars in both arches and the lower left lateral incisor
mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine
Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region
no history of prior dental extractions
an unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated well-defined radiopaque lesion in the left mandibular anterior region
surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, which appeared to obstruct the eruption path of the tooth

concepts.why: The patient has an unerupted lower left lateral incisor, which is a clear indication of tooth impaction.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted tooth, surrounded by a thin radiolucent halo, is consistent with dens in dente.
The patient has a Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region, which is a clear indication of this condition.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted tooth could be an odontoma, which is a type of odontogenic tumor.
The patient has mild spacing between the lower left central incisor and the canine, and crowding in the maxillary anterior region, which is consistent with tooth crowding.
The radiopaque lesion associated with the unerupted tooth could be a supernumerary tooth, which is an extra tooth that is present in addition to the normal complement of teeth.

rationales.F02: The presence of all permanent teeth except the third molars and the lower left lateral incisor suggests tooth impaction.
rationales.F04: Class II, Division 1 malocclusion with crowding in the maxillary anterior region is a strong indicator of Class II malocclusion and tooth crowding.
rationales.F06: The unerupted lower left lateral incisor with an associated radiopaque lesion is highly suggestive of an impacted tooth and possibly an odontoma.
rationales.F07: The radiolucent halo surrounding the radiopaque lesion and obstructing the eruption path of the tooth is a strong indicator of tooth impaction due to an odontogenic lesion.
